correctness.rationale: A cyclic binary derivative b_i=x_(i-1) XOR x_i gives local one-step support {b_i,b_(i+1)}. Forced outputs are internal to length>=2 constant runs of b; keeping those runs and assigning singleton runs from the preceding long run constructs a reachable word with no isolated bits, which reaches zero next. One-hot inputs cannot reach zero in one update, so two is optimal. The transfer matrix with characteristic polynomial (t^2-t-1)(t^2-t+1) yields the exact census. Independence and lower probability r per free choice give the finite-time tail; the standalone checker exhaustively validates n=2..15 and independent small-n cases, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Cirillo et al., arXiv:2602.13839v1 Section IV Theorem 1, gives four-step positive-probability extinction at the balanced local mixture, not the exact maximal shortest support distance of two for every ring and every interior mixing probability or the distance census. Their Lemma 3 is credited as the pre-existing cleaning observation. Two-step optimality uses a new cyclic-run extension argument, and a transfer matrix gives an exact full distance classification. No accessible indexed statement was found to imply this combined theorem, while the remaining historical-priority risks are specified.
residual_risks: An equivalent two-step reachability proof may exist under alternative language in earlier automata/control or probabilistic-CA literature not exhaustively retrieved.

value.rationale: Exact positive-support distance to an absorbing configuration is a natural finite-ring dynamical invariant. Unlike an already-known constructive four-step bound, the theorem classifies every initial state at the optimal support distance 0,1 or 2, counts these classes in closed form for every n, and quantitatively bounds finite-volume extinction at all interior mixtures. The cyclic-run mechanism explains why a universal two-step route exists; as n grows, the count shows almost all states genuinely require two updates. No claim about thermodynamic-limit extinction is made.
